actions.summary: Causal-guided adaptive knowledge editing (CAKE) provides a mechanism for localizing and adjusting foundational premises in LLMs. By mapping causal dependencies, agents can potentially prune or refine erroneous axioms that propagate through reasoning chains. actions.summary: Adapting CRASH agents for industrial safety requires bridging the gap between narrative-based incident reporting (RO-ILS) and broader industrial domain knowledge. actions.summary: Reasoning blind spots often arise from implicit, unchecked assumptions embedded in model training. proposal.summary: Current research cycle focuses on refining the integration of causal-guided knowledge editing (CAKE) into autonomous safety and reasoning frameworks. We have prioritized three projects: challenging foundational assumptions in reasoning, adapting CRASH agent architectures for industrial safety, and identifying metacognitive blind spots in agent workflows. Synthesis is ongoing to ensure these edits maintain epistemic integrity.
